decisions.title: Treat MGA and trauma-informed practice as out of scope for foundational literature
decisions.description: Hoben's AARC overview explicitly maps onto the Mutual Gains Approach (Susskind) and aligns with trauma-informed facilitation. Neither is referenced in the position paper's core framework discussion.
decisions.rationale: The paper's core claim is computational — that CPRI/AARC supplies the missing diagnostic structure for FPO. MGA and trauma-informed facilitation are contextual enrichments about where AARC has been applied, not why it works as a framework. They can be referenced in a later section once the framework is established.

decisions.title: Narrow Clarity to CPRI's content dimension, diverging from Hoben
decisions.description: Hoben's Clarity includes procedural articulation of roles and commitments. The position paper restricts Clarity to shared understanding of the substantive issues in dispute and assigns procedural clarity to Agency.
decisions.rationale: Annotation reliability requires mutual exclusivity. Conflating content and procedural clarity produces overlapping signals that cannot be distinguished. The narrowing is grounded in CPRI's content dimension, which is established literature, and is now explicitly noted in the paper.

decisions.title: Refine AARC component definitions toward Hoben's wording
decisions.description: Acknowledgement, Agency, and Reciprocity definitions in the position paper were revised to incorporate Hoben's framing: affirmation-not-endorsement and psychological safety for Acknowledgement; structural and power asymmetry for Agency; mutual responsibility and shared stake for Reciprocity. Hoben (2020) cited alongside each.
decisions.rationale: The paper's existing definitions were faithful in substance but missed Hoben's normative and structural layers. Adding these terms preserves the operational specificity of the deficit definitions while bringing the paper closer to Hoben's intent — without changing the analytical structure that supports the CPRI mapping and priority ordering.

decisions.title: Cluster face concerns under Acknowledgement in the taxonomy
decisions.description: The RAG output from JIBC practitioner manuals clusters face-saving and face-maintenance material near Reciprocity. The taxonomy draft places face concerns under Acknowledgement, consistent with the position paper's CPRI mapping which assigns identity deficits to Acknowledgement.
decisions.rationale: Hicks (2011), Ting-Toomey (1988), and Goffman (1967) — all in the annotated bibliography — ground face and identity at the relational/identity layer that Acknowledgement addresses. Resolving in favour of this clustering preserves the paper's theoretical architecture and provides a clean operational test (face-preserving reframe distinguishes Acknowledgement from Reciprocity).

decisions.title: Classify the Panama hydropower case as Agency, not Clarity
decisions.description: The JIBC material describes indigenous communities given insufficient data about a hydropower project. Under the taxonomy's scope constraint, this is labeled Agency rather than Clarity.
decisions.rationale: The information gap was a symptom of structural exclusion from the planning process, not a standalone epistemic failure. Classifying it as Clarity would erode the scope constraint separating content from procedural deficits. The case is retained as the canonical Agency vs. Clarity boundary example for annotator training.

decisions.title: Adopt the dialogue window as the annotation unit
decisions.description: The taxonomy treats deficits as patterns accumulating across multiple turns rather than single-utterance triggers. Diagnostic lead-up, repetition loops, speaking-time asymmetry, and paraverbal escalation are all framed at window level.
decisions.rationale: Single-turn classification is insufficient for deficits that manifest as trajectories (repetition escalation, increasing powerless cues, shifting mindset). Window-level annotation is also more robust to noise from isolated cues that would otherwise trigger false positives.

title: Methodology section drafted; AARC framework restructured
context: Session focused on designing and drafting the methodology section of the position paper. Key methodological decisions were made (training approach, label granularity, window size), the AARC framework section was restructured to merge theory and operationalization, three citations were integrated, and the full methodology section was written into the paper.

decisions.title: Label granularity: binary
decisions.description: AARC deficit labels will be binary (present/absent) per component per window.
decisions.rationale: Graded labels introduce annotation complexity and calibration difficulty without theoretical justification for the gradations. Binary labels are standard in deficit annotation and keep the corpus reproducible.

decisions.title: Window size: 5 turns
decisions.description: Annotation unit is the current turn plus four preceding turns.
decisions.rationale: Reciprocity is the most context-dependent component and requires several turns to establish a pattern. Five turns covers all four components reliably while keeping LLM annotation tractable at scale.

decisions.title: Training approach: GRPO-style group ranking
decisions.description: N candidate interventions are generated at each deficit-present window, scored across all four AARC components equally, and ranked by aggregate score. Pairwise preference pairs are derived from the ranking.
decisions.rationale: Binary DPO pairs collapse the multi-component reward structure. Group ranking captures preference intensity and preserves per-component scoring, producing a richer training signal appropriate to a four-component framework.

decisions.title: Equal weighting across AARC components
decisions.description: The aggregate score at each intervention point is an unweighted sum across the four component scores.
decisions.rationale: No empirical basis yet exists for differential weighting. Equal weighting is defensible and keeps the methodology conventional. Whether the diagnostic priority ordering warrants weighting is deferred to future work.

decisions.title: Standalone AARC framework
decisions.description: The proposed framework is not an extension of FPO but a replacement for it in the mediation context. Clarity inherits FPO epistemic submodels (Unc, Contr) as its operational basis.
decisions.rationale: A standalone framework is a cleaner and more defensible contribution than a patch on FPO. Borrowing Clarity components from FPO provides grounding without architectural entanglement.

decisions.title: AARC section restructured
decisions.description: The original AARC Components section was renamed and restructured to merge theoretical definitions with operationalization content into one unified section per component. RAG pipeline description moved before component descriptions.
decisions.rationale: The prior structure duplicated content across the theoretical and methodology sections. One place for each component eliminates redundancy and improves readability.

decisions.rationale: Operationalizing the ordering requires trajectory-level corpus design that adds significant complexity. Deferred to future work (FPO-q23).

decisions.title: Intervention appropriateness scoring: ternary scale per component
decisions.description: Each candidate intervention is scored +1 (targets a detected deficit), -1 (worsens a non-deficit component), or 0 (neutral) across all four AARC components. Aggregate = unweighted sum; group ranked by aggregate.
decisions.rationale: Directly operationalizes the position paper scoring procedure; ternary scale captures both positive contribution and iatrogenic harm without requiring a separate harm metric.

decisions.title: Worsens (-1) defined as next-turn observable signal
decisions.description: An intervention worsens a non-deficit component if the immediately following turn contains an observable signal from that component's deficit signal list. Single signal suffices; delayed effects score 0.
decisions.rationale: Strict next-turn scope keeps the label observable and falsifiable; delayed attribution is too confounded to score reliably.

decisions.title: Repair labeling requires positive engagement indicator
decisions.description: Absence-based resolution indicators are only labeled as repaired when the deficit signal is absent AND at least one positive engagement indicator from the same component's resolution list is present in the same window.
decisions.rationale: Absence alone is ambiguous between repair and withdrawal; requiring a positive confirmation signal makes repair labels reliable.

decisions.title: v1 scope is dyadic only
decisions.description: All signal definitions, resolution indicators, and intervention mappings are specified for two-party mediation. Multi-party facilitation deferred to a future version.
decisions.rationale: Corpus construction and signal definitions are substantially simpler in the dyadic case; multi-party dynamics introduce coalition and speaking-order complexity that would expand scope significantly.

decisions.rationale: Provides a second independent line of evidence for why content-only intervention is insufficient: a party in physiological flooding cannot productively process epistemic correction regardless of its accuracy.

context: Session focused on expanding annotation diversity and optimizing the GPT-5.4 annotator via DSPy MiPROv2. decisions.title: MiPROv2 light (accuracy metric) is best optimization result to date
decisions.rationale: Macro-F1 0.505 (Ack:0.769, Aga:0.400, Rec:0.600, Cla:0.250). Medium run gamed accuracy metric via Clarity suppression (Cla F1=0.000). Recall-weighted metric fix did not resolve Clarity either — root cause is missing taxonomy, not metric formulation.

decisions.title: Clarity failure is a grounding problem, not a data or metric problem

decisions.rationale: Qwen2.5 32B needs ~24-26GB including KV cache at 16K context — too tight. 14B fits comfortably. Must set num_ctx=20000 per-request. OpenAI-compatible API. Updated FPO-68z with findings.
